key_insight: Step‑Decomposed Influence (SDI) breaks a single training‑data influence score into a length‑τ vector aligned with each recurrent iteration, revealing when (which loop step) a training example actually affects a looped transformer’s computation.
problem_solved: Existing influence estimators (e.g., TracIn) aggregate influence across all recurrent iterations, hiding the temporal/iteration structure of influence in looped transformers and preventing step‑level attribution and debugging.
method: Derive SDI by decomposing the TracIn influence score into per‑iteration contributions across the τ recurrent applications of the shared block.
Compute a length‑τ influence trace for each training example (instead of a single scalar), enabling identification of which iteration(s) drive the influence.
Provide practical computation strategy and diagnostics to visualize and compare per‑step contributions for target examples and datasets.
impact: SDI gives practitioners fine‑grained, step‑level attribution useful for debugging, dataset curation, targeted data editing, and understanding where and when training data steer latent reasoning in looped transformers.
visual_elements: Schematic of a looped transformer showing a single shared block applied τ times with arrows labeled by step index (1..τ).
Example per‑step influence vector: a horizontal bar/line plot showing influence magnitude across steps for one training example.
Heatmap (steps × training examples) highlighting which examples matter at which iterations.
Workflow diagram: compute SDI → visualize top per‑step influencers → apply targeted data edits or diagnostics.
paper_title: Step-resolved data attribution for looped transformers
paper_authors: Georgios Kaissis, David Mildenberger, Juan Felipe Gomez, Martin J. Menten, Eleni Triantafillou
